titulo: Rome's coin went from 98% silver to 2% 🏛️
descripcion: The denarius was almost pure silver under Augustus. By around 270 AD, the main coin was copper with a silver wash. This is what ancient inflation looks like. Series: How Empires Fall.

escenas.texto: Rome's money went from almost pure silver to almost pure copper. This is what it looks like when an empire prints money.
Around the time of Augustus, the denarius was about ninety eight percent silver.
But the army kept getting more expensive. The Severan emperors doubled a soldier's base pay. And there was no new silver.
The fix? Melt the coins, add copper, mint more. By around two seventy, the main coin was about two percent silver.
With weaker coins, sellers asked for more of them. Prices rose, and the empire fell into fifty years of chaos.
Sound familiar? Follow for the series: how empires fall.
